== The Marvelous Land of Oz ==

Tip is a youth of the Country of the Gillikins, in the North of the Land of Oz. Old Mombi, his guardian, sometimes calls him by his longer name, Tippetarius, though he is known simply as Tip. He is also known as Ozma, or Princess Ozma. Tip remembers nothing of his own parents; he was brought to Mombi while still quite young and raised by her, though her reputation was far from good.

Restless and fond of mischief, Tip built a figure from a carved pumpkin and wooden limbs, naming it Jack Pumpkinhead, and hauled it to the bend in the road to give old Mombi a fright. When Mombi later threatened to turn him into a marble statue, Tip refused to accept such a fate. He gathered bread and cheese, took a pepper-box holding the Powder of Life from her basket, and slipped away at night with Jack.

On the road, Tip cared for his companions: he repaired Jack's wooden joints whenever they gave way, and after bringing an old sawhorse to life as the Saw-Horse, he whittled it a pair of ears from bark so it could hear his commands. When a ferryman refused to carry the travelers across a river without payment, the group crossed on their own and continued on toward the Emerald City, the grass and trees turning from lavender to green as they neared it.

Upon reaching the Emerald City, Tip presented Jack Pumpkinhead to His Majesty the Scarecrow, and it was there confirmed, in answer to Jellia's question, that Tip was the one who had made Jack.

=== Events ===

* Tip, a Gillikin youth whose full name is Tippetarius, lives in the North of Oz under guardian old Mombi, a woman suspected of magical arts.
* Tip remembers nothing of his parents and was raised by Mombi since early childhood.
* Tip does chores for Mombi (wood, corn-fields, pigs, milking) but slacks off and plays whenever her view is blocked.
* Tip openly hates Mombi and shows little respect for her.
* While Mombi is away for two days buying groceries, Tip carves a pumpkin into a jolly face intending to scare her.
* Tip builds a wooden body from saplings and bark, joints it with pegs, and fashions a neck to hold the pumpkin head.
* Tip dresses the finished figure in clothes found in Mombi's chest and names him 'Jack Pumpkinhead.'
* Tip carries his pumpkin-headed man Jack to the bend in the road, repairing a fallen-off arm and twisted head along the way, to scare old Mombi.
* Mombi first mistakes Jack for a real man, then recognizes Tip's trick after noticing his carved pumpkin head.
* Deciding to test one of her new powders instead of punishing Tip, Mombi sprinkles the Powder of Life on Jack and speaks magic words over him.
* Jack Pumpkinhead comes to life, delighting Mombi and amazing the hidden, watching Tip.
* Mombi catches Tip laughing, drags him home, and locks Jack in the cow stable for the night.
* At the farmhouse, Mombi brews a potion of milk, vinegar, herbs, and powders, revealing she intends to turn Tip into a marble statue for her garden.
* Tip pleads and bargains against the transformation, but Mombi insists, sets the kettle to cool, and orders him to bed at midnight while she plans to complete the spell at daybreak.
* Tip decides to run away from Mombi rather than be turned into a marble statue.
* Tip returns to the cow-stable to free Jack Pumpkinhead, whom he considers his own creation.
* Tip and Jack travel through the night and into morning, taking a winding path to avoid pursuit.
* They stop to rest, where Jack realizes Tip is his creator and calls him father.
* Tip explains the geography of Oz's regions and their colors, and recounts Dorothy's story and the Wizard's departure.
* Tip tells Jack that the Scarecrow now rules the Emerald City, and they decide to travel there.
* Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead continue their journey, with Jack worrying his wooden joints will wear out from walking.
* Jack tries to sit down on an old sawhorse but his joints give way and he collapses; Tip repairs him and tells him to remain standing from then on.
* Tip and Jack debate whether the sawhorse resembles a real horse, discussing its tree-trunk body, branch tail, knot eyes, and carved mouth.
* Tip remembers he still carries the magic Powder of Life in the pepper-box that animated Jack.
* Tip decides to try reviving the sawhorse so Jack can ride it and spare his joints.
* Tip recalls and repeats the words and hand gestures he secretly observed old Mombi use, sprinkling the powder on the sawhorse.
* The sawhorse comes to life, stretching its legs and yawning, astonishing Tip while Jack praises him as a clever sorcerer.
* The Saw-Horse ignores Tip's shouted 'Whoa' until Jack points out it has no ears to hear with.
* Tip whittles ears from tree bark and fastens them to the Saw-Horse's head.
* Tip rights the Saw-Horse, repairs a broken ear, and teaches it the commands Whoa, Get-Up, and Trot.
* Tip explains they are traveling to the Emerald City to see the Scarecrow, with Jack riding on the Saw-Horse's back.
* Tip carves and hammers a wooden post into the Saw-Horse's back for Jack to hold onto while riding.
* Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead resume their journey toward the Emerald City atop the Saw-Horse.
* A ferryman refuses to row them across a river because Tip has no money.
* Tip rides the Saw-Horse across the river while Jack wades and holds the horse's tail; all get wet.
* Tip runs behind the galloping Saw-Horse holding its tail, but the branch breaks and he is left behind on the road.
* Unaware Tip fell behind, Jack and the Saw-Horse race on and arrive at the green wall of the Emerald City.
* Tip walks toward Emerald City, grows hungry after eating his rations.
* Tip follows Jinjur to a forest clearing where 400 girls, armed with knitting needles, assemble in four companies by home region (Munchkin, Quadling, Winkie, Gillikin).
* Tip follows the Soldier with the Green Whiskers to the palace, arriving before news spreads that the girl army has conquered the Emerald City.
* Tip warns the Scarecrow the girls plan to make a rag carpet of his outside and stuff cushions with his straw, prompting him to plan an escape.
* The Scarecrow has the Saw-Horse (locked in the treasury as a supposed jewel) brought out, and he, Tip, and Jack Pumpkinhead mount it, tied together with a clothesline, leaving the Royal Army behind.
* Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Pumpkinhead Jack are dunked in a river when the Saw-Horse struggles while carrying them across.
* Tip calms the horse, cuts the riders free, and finds the Scarecrow collapsed on the bank with his straw soaked and displaced.
* Jack's pumpkin head has been swept downstream; Tip retrieves it with a long pole and reattaches it to his neck.
* Tip dries the Scarecrow's straw in the sun and restuffs him back into proper shape.
* At nightfall the tired, hungry Tip lies down to sleep using the Scarecrow as a pillow while his companions, needing no rest, keep watch.
* Tip and the Scarecrow's party reach the City of the Winkies and its Emperor's palace.
* The Tin Woodman welcomes Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, and explains the engraved star on his chest covers the patch where the Wizard placed his heart.
* The Woggle-Bug argues that puns display superior education, irritating Tip and drawing a warning from the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman to restrain himself.
* Jinjur threatens to destroy each companion in a gruesome way, while ordering Tip returned to old Mombi.
* Tip reports from the window that girl soldiers surround the palace, confirming they remain prisoners despite driving Jinjur out earlier.
* Tip's Powder of Life falls from his pocket, and he explains it can bring anything to life but only one dose remains.
* Tip worries the magic powder is running low and must decide whether to animate the head or the legs of the sofas.
* The Scarecrow argues the head is more important than the legs since the Thing will fly, not walk, so Tip sprinkles the remaining powder on the head.
* Tip speaks the magic words he learned from Mombi, and the Thing comes to life, screeching and flapping its wings violently.
* Tip commands the Gump to return, and because its head was brought to life, it obeys and lands safely back on the roof.
* Tip explains to the newly-animated Gump-headed Thing that it exists to carry the group through the air.
* The Gump flies south with Tip, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, Woggle-Bug, and Saw-Horse aboard.
* Tip finds a false bottom in the discarded pepper-box holding three of Dr. Nikidik's silver wishing pills, useless because the instructions require counting seventeen by twos.
* Hearing the Jackdaws returning, Scarecrow has Tip and the Woggle-Bug hide, Jack's head laid down, and his own straw scattered over them for protection just as the angry birds attack.
* Tip suggests restuffing the Scarecrow with the money found in the nest, which the Jackdaws had stolen from towns over the years, and the group refills him with bills of various denominations.
* Tip swallows the first pill and, in pain, wishes he had never swallowed it, which undoes the act and returns all three pills to the box.
* Glinda reveals that the true heir to the Emerald City throne is Ozma, daughter of the former King Pastoria, hidden away by the Wizard with old Mombi's help.
* Glinda resolves to march her army on the Emerald City to capture Mombi and force her to reveal where Ozma is hidden.
* Glinda tells the assembled group she has failed to find Mombi and fears the expedition to rescue Ozma will fail.
* Glinda pursues the Griffin on the tireless Saw-Horse while Tip and the others follow by air aboard the Gump.
* Glinda demands Mombi reveal what happened to the infant Ozma, whom the Wizard hid with her years ago.
* Mombi admits the Wizard gave her the baby Ozma in exchange for teaching her magic tricks.
* Mombi reveals she transformed the girl Ozma into a boy, and points to Tip as that transformed child.
* Tip is shocked and reluctant, wishing to remain a boy and continue traveling with his friends.
* Glinda refuses to allow Mombi to reverse the transformation later, calling it dishonest magic, and orders Mombi to restore Tip's true form now.
* Mombi performs the transformation ritual, and Tip emerges as the beautiful Princess Ozma, to the amazement of all.
* Queen Jinjur despairs on learning Mombi confessed and that Tip is truly Princess Ozma.
* Jinjur refuses to give up her throne and declares war on Glinda and Ozma.
* Glinda, Ozma, the Scarecrow and a small guard fly the Gump into the palace courtyard and capture Jinjur.
* The Army of Revolt surrenders, stolen jewels are returned, and Ozma is crowned queen of the Emerald City.
* The Gump asks to be dismantled back into its original parts, and Ozma grants its wish.

== Narrative role ==

Tip is a Gillikin youth living in the North of Oz as ward of old Mombi, an old woman suspected of practicing magic. He remembers nothing of his parents, having been raised by Mombi since early childhood, and is set to daily chores — cutting wood, tending the corn-fields, keeping pigs, and milking — from which he regularly slacks off to play whenever Mombi's attention is elsewhere. Using branches and clothing found in Mombi's chest, he builds and dresses a figure he names Jack Pumpkinhead.

Later, Tip runs behind the galloping Saw-Horse while holding onto its tail, but the branch he grips breaks and he is left behind on the road. Afterward, when Jack's pumpkin head is swept downstream, Tip retrieves it with a long pole and reattaches it to Jack's neck.

When Jinjur threatens to destroy each of the companions in gruesome fashion, she orders that Tip be returned to old Mombi. Around this time, Tip's Powder of Life falls from his pocket, and he explains that it can bring anything to life but that only one dose remains.

Tip speaks the magic words he learned from Mombi, and the Thing comes to life, screeching and flapping its wings violently. Worried that the powder is running low, he must decide whether to animate the head or the legs of the sofas; he then commands the Gump to return, and because its head has been brought to life, it obeys and lands safely back on the roof.

Tip explains to the newly animated Gump-headed Thing that it exists to carry the group through the air. He also discovers a false bottom in the discarded pepper-box, holding three of Dr. Nikidik's silver wishing pills — useless, since the instructions require counting seventeen by twos. When Jackdaws' stolen money is found in their nest, Tip suggests restuffing the Scarecrow with it, and the group refills him with bills of various denominations.

Old Mombi eventually admits that the Wizard gave her a baby named Ozma in exchange for teaching her magic tricks — an admission that reveals Tip to be that child, also known as Princess Ozma. When Jinjur refuses to give up her throne and declares war on Glinda the Good and Ozma, the Army of Revolt ultimately surrenders and the stolen jewels are returned; Ozma is crowned queen of the Emerald City, and Jinjur despairs on learning that Mombi has confessed and that Tip is truly Princess Ozma.

== Personality ==

Tip is mischievous and inventive, drawn to testing "the cleverness of his workmanship" rather than to strict practicality; he builds Jack Pumpkinhead expressly to frighten old Mombi and takes evident satisfaction in seeing the trick succeed. This same restless curiosity shows in his willingness to experiment — first with the Powder of Life, later by whittling a pair of ears for the newly awakened Saw-Horse when the creature fails to heed a shouted "Whoa!"

He also shows a rebellious streak toward authority: faced with the prospect of "being a marble statue," he resolves, rebelliously, that "I'm not going to stand it," and admits in private that he "never did like that old woman," Mombi, wondering "how I ever came to live with her." Yet Tip is not merely defiant — he is attentive and conscientious toward what he creates. When Jack's joints give way and he crashes to the ground, Tip rushes to him, straightens his limbs, and checks his head for cracks, and he later regrets not having "constructed the wooden limbs more carefully and substantially." He also proves patient with Jack's oddities, choosing to let the Pumpkinhead call him "father" rather than undertake "another long and tedious explanation." Confronted with sudden mishap, such as the Saw-Horse's wild circling that leaves him "dancing away in pain," Tip reacts with alarm but responds practically, seeking a workable fix rather than giving in to panic.

== Appearance ==

Tip is described as a boy of small and delicate build, a detail noted when Jack Pumpkinhead addresses him as "father."

== Powers ==

Tip has no innate magical ability, but shows real skill as a craftsman: he assembles a pumpkin-headed man whose jointed limbs are sturdy enough to walk, working the leg joints by hand until they hold together, and takes visible pride in testing "the cleverness of his workmanship." His capacity to bring a creation to life depends on the Powder of Life, a substance he takes rather than one he possesses by nature — his gift lies in construction and resourceful use of found materials, not in sorcery of his own.

== Trivia ==

* Old Mombi addressed Tip by his full name, Tippetarius, though the shorter name was used by everyone else.
* When the newly animated Saw-Horse ignored Tip's shouted commands to stop, Jack Pumpkinhead pointed out that the creature had no ears; Tip then whittled a pair from tree bark and fastened them to its head.
* A ferryman refused to row Tip and his companions across the river on the road to the Emerald City because Tip carried no money.
* Tip built Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden joints himself; by the time they reached the Emerald City, the purple trousers, pink waistcoat, and red shirt still hung loosely over the joints he had constructed.
